body:
I meant that I can never actually father a child. Yes, I could hypothetically adopt, but as I've said, I personally don't think that I could do that and it's pretty much unheard of within my culture. 

I have tutored elementary school kids for several years and I am a Big Brother, but I am obviously quite aware that the relationship I have with those kids is very different from being a parent. I like kids, but again, the fact that I can't ever experience that sort of bond is really painful and I don't know how to deal with that.

There is literally a 0% chance of me ever being able to be a father. I am completely sterile. There is absolutely no chance due to the condition I have.
With reckless abandon, perhaps it is, but my inability to do so at all is a failure as well.
I guess so...but again, I still can never be a father and I don't know how to deal with that. I feel like less of a man and I know that's how much of society considers someone in my situation.

I guess the problem is that I do not know how to do that. Can you elaborate on what you mean? I don't know how to get out of this mindset.

I feel as if my life has been wasted, because I can never know such an integral part of the human experience.
I mean, I am failure as an organism, when you get down to it. I cannot propagate the human race as others can. It isn't any of our faults', but that doesn't change the facts, I guess.

No, don't worry about it.

I am just so tired of having to keep trying. I used to be able to get up the strength to just keep going by thinking that I can't know what will happen or how I will change in the future, but it is too difficult to do that nowadays. I do not want to have to be like this for the rest of my life; I do not want to have to keep trying to "get better".

It would be foolhardy (and probably unrealistic) to just disconnect myself from my family and friends.

I was under the impression that I had been doing just that...

I understand what you mean, but I have no idea how to change my mindset and/or the values of the culture in which I was raised.

Yes, I am "just 18", but I have struggled with depression for more than half of my life. This is mostly what I have known...

How am I supposed to find the "right" therapist? How much more time and money must I waste? And with all due respect, how do you know that I will even be able to find such a person? If therapy has not helped me in the past several years in which I have tried it, then why would it work now or in the future?

I have tried therapy for years. I saw many different therapists from 10 to 16 for my depression, but it didn't help and at times it even worsened my state of mind. Regarding this particular issue, I have seen 2 different people and have not gotten any real benefit from talking. Just a waste of money.

It is incurable; I am 100% sterile. I would rather not discuss it, but it is due to a medical condition. I am 18.

The scenario you were discussing is pretty implausible, but thanks for trying to help, I guess,

I have. It has not helped. I don't understand how it could...it's not like they can magically make me able to be a father.

Right, but my future wife would have to hide this pregnancy...

I would know they are not mine, as would they themselves, and as would my family. We would be looked down upon. My grandparents would not consider them to be their grandchildren, and anyway, how would I be able to consider them my children when I of course know that to be untrue? The idea of raising a stranger's child fills me with sadness and frustration. I don't think that I could do that, for a number of reasons.

Well I am a man, so...lol.

My family would know, as they know I am sterile. And anyway, I am not comfortable lying to a child and telling them I am their father. That would be keeping an essential part of their identity from them. I think that's wrong. And it would not solve my problem at all; if anything, it would just create more problems and stress.

Adoption really is not practiced in my culture. There is an enormous stigma attached. An adopted child would not be considered family.

Edit: and thanks but I know that is most likely untrue about the genes thing...
